**Test image observations:**
- Soybean leaf with a large, irregular, dark brown necrotic lesion
- Lesion covers a substantial portion of the upper leaf area
- No distinct small-spot pattern; single large blotch
- Some yellowing visible on background leaves
- No white/powdery coating, no pustules, no waterlogged halo

**Analysis:**
The Bacterial_Blight reference shows small, scattered, angular yellow-brown lesions — quite different from the large single necrotic blotch in the test image.

The test image's large, irregular dark-brown necrotic area on a soybean leaf, combined with yellowing on surrounding vegetation, is most consistent with **Phytophthora** leaf blight — which produces large, irregular brown lesions that can expand across much of the leaf blade, often with associated plant yellowing.

This doesn't match:
- Bacterial_Blight (small angular scattered lesions)
- Septoria_brown_spot (multiple smaller irregular spots)
- Frogeye_leaf_spot (small circular spots with gray centers)
- Powdery_Mildew (white powdery coating)
